featured_reviews.name: Falguni P
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kids Friendly place.
This place is divided into different sections, the entry is free.

*Fish park - this park is quite big and has 3 gates,
The first half has fish tanks, selfie point and a fountain
Currently there are only few fishes, the fountain is shut and the empty tanks are not maintained well (due to COVID)

*The cricket ground - usually there is local cricket match on weekends, chairs are provided for audience.

*Kids play area- there are slides, swings, and play area for kids.

*Open Gym- they have a gym area near the second gate, which is currently closed for public, equipments are mainted nicely.

*Walking / jogging track - there is a long walking and jogging track around the park, local residents usually come visit for morning and evening walks

*Accessibility - park is partially Accessibility as there are stairs in some parts of the park. This place is ideal for kids, family and senior citizens.
The fish park gate is accessible but to reach the other area it is ideal to use the second gate which has a slope.

featured_reviews.name: Cletus Dias
featured_reviews.review_text: The Fish Park was one of my favorite park for walks. Over the years and especially after the pandemic, it has lost its charm. A lot of maintenance is required, tanks are empty and dirty. Unfortunately, people don't respect free places like this and don't support keeping it clean.

featured_reviews.name: Savita Prabhune
featured_reviews.review_text: There are about 10 acquariums. But they need cleaning. The park needs to be maintained. There are fibre decorations in the park those were full of dust. There are selfie points but in dark there is very less light. The acquariums need cleaning and the glass needs wiping.

featured_reviews.name: Lloyd D'souza
featured_reviews.review_text:
The fish park leaves a lot to be desired. There are tanks and there are fish. Neither in the best shape. It’s a wonder the fish are surviving. Needs urgent maintenance.

Entry is free and there is a whole other section with a nice walking track. It’s quiet and peaceful given the location, right next to a busy road and the new metro station.

featured_reviews.name: Divya
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently attended a wedding at Kora Kendar, and while the overall ambience was pleasant, I was disappointed with the lack of proper washroom facilities. Having previously visited for a garba event a few years ago, I expected improvements in this area, but unfortunately, it was still a major inconvenience.

The venue relies on portable restrooms, commonly known as porta-potties, which are known for their discomfort and lack of cleanliness. This arrangement was highly inconvenient, especially during a wedding where guests require comfortable and hygienic washroom facilities. The absence of proper washroom amenities significantly affected the overall experience.

However, it's worth noting that Kora Kendar does excel in terms of ambiance. The atmosphere created for the event was enjoyable, and the management seemed to have put effort into creating a pleasant environment for the guests. The overall decor and arrangements were satisfactory, contributing to the positive aspects of the venue.

Despite the shortcomings in washroom facilities, Kora Kendar may still be a suitable choice for events like garba or weddings, provided that alternative arrangements are made for washroom facilities. It would greatly enhance the overall experience and ensure the comfort of guests.

featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh Bandivadekar
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Taste of Konkan in Borivali and had a wonderful experience. We tried the Kolhapuri Mutton Thali, Surmai Fish Thali and Stuffed Bombil Fry and every dish was packed with authentic flavours. The mutton was perfectly cooked with a rich, spicy gravy, while the Surmai was fresh and served in a generous portion. The Stuffed Bombil Fry was crispy and absolutely delicious. The ambience was warm and welcoming, making the overall dining experience even better. Definitely a great place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Konkani food in Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Vikram Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Taste of Konkan 🐟✨
Fair prices, authentic Konkani flavours, and a warm welcome with kokam sarbat & papad 👌
Surmai thali (₹700) stole the show with 3 crispy fried pieces 🤌
Prawns thali (₹525) was decent, could be better…
Stuffed Pomfret (₹800) — filling and flavourful.
Overall, a proper Konkan-style meal worth trying!

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: anish tatkare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I went to this hotel with my family for a dinner.
The hotel's name is only Taste of Konkan, but there is no taste of Konkan anywhere. I'm from Konkan. So don't fool people by talking about the taste of Konkan.
The chicken thali only had the taste of Elaichi and nothing else. Same with Prawns thali too. Bombil Bhaji was of a lower standard than Onion Bhaji.

featured_reviews.name: Tejas Khandalekar
featured_reviews.review_text: We enjoyed the food. Prawns thali and Kombadi vade was great options which we enjoyed. Prawns curry, Prawns masala was so delicious. Sol kadhi was also tasty. In kombadi vade, curry was perfectly Malvani taste and vade was crunchy and yummy. However, bombil bhaji (pakoda) was not that great. Overall food was good, ambience was also good

featured_reviews.name: Sushil Malik
featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: priyanka mustafi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good food, quite authentic in taste. We had prawn manchow soup which was loaded with prawns. Their prawn lollypops are great, we also had squid tawa masala which was a bit salty but well cooked. We ordered thalis which was the main aim. Surmai and pomfret. The size was very good and fish was fresh. The thali was very good - rice, bhakri ( u can choose amboli or even chapati) , bhurji, sukka, prawn curry, bangda curry, salad and ofcourse rawa fry of the fish you choose. The place is very tiny with only 8 tables but service is prompt and nice ambience for a homely meal
.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

featured_reviews.name: Hillary DSouza
featured_reviews.review_text: This market offers variety of fresh fish eg.  White Snapper, Pomfrets, Rawas, Kingfish, Mackrels and Prawns. Lots of variety in small fishes also.
